payments.title: A payments platform with 21 services
payments.summary: A payments system split into Node and Java services, wired straight into partner banks, with web and mobile products running on top of those same services.

highlights.1: Domain split into independent services (IAM, wallet, orders, payments, receivables, tax, notifications) with distinct gateways for the admin console and the end customer.
highlights.2: Dedicated Java/Spring services for Pix, bank slips, receivables, and invoice issuing, isolating each banking integration from the product core.
highlights.3: A Next.js console and a React Native app on the same services, with CI/CD on Docker, PM2, and GitHub Actions.

edtech.title: White-label apps for schools
edtech.summary: A single codebase produces independent apps per institution — branding, bundle, integrations, and features all defined by tenant configuration.

highlights.1: A tenant registry driving both build time (bundle ID, icon, splash) and runtime (theme, LMS URL, feature flags) from one source.
highlights.2: Continuous Android and iOS releases with Expo/EAS plus OTA updates triggered by pushes to the main branch.
highlights.3: NestJS backends covering auth, cloud files, push, and email, alongside Next.js admin consoles and the Ionic/Angular mobile LMS.

spectroscopy.title: Botanical identification SaaS driven by spectroscopy
spectroscopy.summary: A platform wiring a near-infrared scanner to statistical identification models, with the same interface running in the browser and on the desktop.

highlights.1: A Next.js PWA as the single source of UI, also packaged inside a Tauri/Rust desktop shell that bridges the hardware.
highlights.2: NestJS microservices behind a single gateway, with per-institution data isolation through PostgreSQL row level security.
highlights.3: A monorepo with its own design system, typed HTTP contracts, and Storybook as the living UI reference.

realestate.title: Real-estate SaaS platform
realestate.summary: CRM, operations, property catalog, and client portal on a multi-tenant microservice architecture.

highlights.1: NestJS services communicating over gRPC behind an API Gateway, with contracts versioned in a shared package.
highlights.2: Domain modeling for properties, deals, and brokers, with per-tenant authorization and data isolation.
highlights.3: A pnpm + Turborepo monorepo whose domain, UI, and config packages are reused across backend and frontend.

ai-workflow.title: AI in the engineering workflow
ai-workflow.description: I work AI-first. Not faster autocomplete — the engineering process redesigned around agents, held to the same rigor as any system in production.

spec-driven.title: Spec and plan before code
spec-driven.description: Any change of substance starts from a spec that pins down the problem, the constraints and the acceptance criteria, and from a plan broken into verifiable tasks, each with its own test. An ambiguous spec is a requirements bug: cheaper to fix there than thirty files later.

orchestration.title: Each phase on the right model
orchestration.description: Planning, implementing, debugging and reviewing are different jobs, and models are not equally good at all four. Each phase is routed to the one that performs best on it, and whoever writes the plan is not the one implementing it. Execution stays sequential and isolated: one task at a time, on its own branch.

context.title: Project standards, versioned
context.description: Module layout, logging and testing conventions live in the repository as executable instructions, reviewed in PRs like anything else. A new agent inherits the rule instead of guessing; when the rule changes, it changes for everyone in the same commit.

tooling.title: Tooling over a protocol
tooling.description: The agent reads the task board, the database, the browser and CI over MCP, instead of relying on context pasted by hand. It trades “what I remember about the system” for “what the system just answered”.

verification.title: Evidence before claims
verification.description: A failing test before the implementation; lint, typecheck, coverage and end-to-end runs in CI as an objective gate. A test that depends on timing, or that checks implementation instead of behavior, gets rewritten — never labeled flaky and ignored.

review.title: Human review at the merge
review.description: I read everything that comes back before opening the PR. Agents speed up producing code and, with it, producing wrong code — the gain is in the gates that catch it early, not in trusting more.

ai-workflow.footnote: Applied to real products, not demos: this is how I moved a six-person squad to a spec-driven flow in edtech, and how I build a microservice SaaS platform for the real estate market today.

oniapp.description: Study app for schools that run on Moodle. Each institution gets its own app in the stores, with its own brand and colors, but all of them come from a single codebase. Students sign in with their school account and reach courses, files, and announcements from the phone.
oniapp.role: Tech Lead and full stack developer. I designed the system that turns one codebase into one app per school, wrote the app in React Native with Expo, and handle the App Store and Play Store releases through EAS.

oniapp-api.description: The API behind the student app. It handles sign-in, talks to each school’s Moodle, stores every client’s settings, and keeps a record of what changes in the system.
oniapp-api.role: Tech Lead and full stack developer. I wrote the NestJS modules, modeled the MySQL database with TypeORM, and left docs and logs the team actually uses day to day.

oniapp-admin.description: Panel where the Onilearning team and each partner school configure their own app: logo, colors, which features are on, who has access, and the history of changes.

seja-api.description: The API behind the wellbeing app: accounts and social sign-in, content tracks, user progress, push delivery, and cloud file storage.
